payload.name: Breakage-Enumeration Synonym Expansion
payload.description: When a question asks what things/items someone had broken or damaged and initial retrieval returns no direct 'broken' memory, use this to expand search terms before answering.
content: When a question asks what kinds of things a person had broken or damaged (e.g., 'what broke down', 'what was damaged', 'what things did X have broken'), do not conclude 'no information' after one literal search; supporting memories may use 'broke down', 'breakdown', 'accident', 'malfunction', 'issue', 'damaged', or 'repair'.

Run additional keyword or structured searches combining the person's name with breakage synonyms (broke, broken, broke down, breakdown, accident, malfunction, damage, issue, repair) and likely object categories (car, vehicle, bike, phone, appliance, device).
Check sufficiency after each search; continue until no new distinct broken/damaged items appear, and cite only memories that explicitly state an item was broken, damaged, or broke down.

solves: The Access agent answered 'no information' after a single literal search for 'broken' even though a memory stated Evan's new Prius 'broke down'. The reusable failure is premature no-info on enumerative damage questions when memory wording differs from query wording. This skill applies to future questions asking what things/items a person had broken, damaged, or had fail, requiring synonym expansion and sufficiency checks before concluding no evidence.
